findings.evidence: "The stipend clock resumes on their first day back."
findings.fix: Clarify whether "stipend clock" refers to the benefit year cycle, and explicitly state whether employees can claim again in the same benefit year after returning from leave, or must wait until the next benefit year.
findings.violation: It's unclear what "stipend clock" means and whether employees who already used their stipend before taking leave would be eligible for another one after returning.

findings.evidence: "However, an incomplete request pauses the timeline until the missing item arrives."
findings.fix: Replace "missing item" with either "missing documentation" or "required information" and clarify what specifically is needed for the request to proceed.
findings.violation: "Missing item" is ambiguous - it's unclear whether this refers to missing documentation or missing equipment - and "arrives" suggests physical equipment, which doesn't align with a reimbursement process.

findings.evidence: "A photo of the receipt is enough for most requests."
findings.fix: Either specify what additional documentation is required for requests that don't meet the "most requests" category, or replace "most" with "all" if a photo is always sufficient.
findings.violation: The phrase "most requests" implies other requests have different requirements, but those alternative requirements are never specified.

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Rewrite in third person: "Employees must keep their equipment in good working condition and the company may request a brief photo check once a year."
findings.location: Restrictions and Exceptions section, first paragraph
findings.violation: This sentence uses second-person pronouns ("You," "we") while the rest of the document uses third person, creating inconsistent voice.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form... Also, you submit the request in the portal. You track its status there until the payment clears."
findings.fix: Rewrite in third person: "Employees record the stipend item on the request form... Employees submit the request in the portal and track its status there until the payment clears."
findings.location: Terminology Notes section, first two sentences
findings.violation: Multiple sentences use second-person pronouns ("You") inconsistently with the document's third-person voice throughout.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: Either expand this section to include all steps outlined in "How to Apply" (start request, save draft, review summary, submit), or remove it and refer readers to "How to Apply."
findings.violation: The section is titled "Request Steps" (plural) but lists only fragments and doesn't provide a complete ordered list, while "How to Apply" earlier outlines a more detailed process.

findings.evidence: "The finance liaison publishes the equipment catalog at the start of the fiscal year. Every entry carries a date stamp so the record stays easy to audit."
findings.fix: Rename the section to reflect its content (e.g., "Equipment Catalog Details") or move this information to "Program Overview" where equipment tracking is introduced, then either provide actual special-case content or remove the section.
findings.violation: The section title "Special Cases" suggests exceptions or unusual circumstances, but the content describes routine equipment catalog publication, which is not a special case.

findings.evidence: "The finance office reviews every stipend request over 200 dollars before it pays out."
findings.fix: Clarify the sequence by specifying when the finance office review occurs relative to manager approval (e.g., "After manager approval, the finance office reviews...").
findings.violation: The approval sequence is unclear - it's not stated whether this finance office review occurs before, after, or in parallel with the manager review mentioned in "Approval Timeline."

findings.evidence: "The finance office also flags any request that repeats within the same quarter."
findings.fix: Specify the consequence of flagging a repeated request (e.g., "...and may require additional documentation" or "...and the request may be denied").
findings.violation: The policy states repeated requests are flagged but never specifies what happens as a result - whether the request is denied, requires additional justification, or is simply noted.

findings.evidence: "The benefits team reviews the equipment catalog at the start of the fiscal year."
findings.fix: Remove this sentence or consolidate all equipment catalog review information into a single location in the document.
findings.violation: This statement repeats information already mentioned in "Program Overview" and "Special Cases," creating redundancy.
